appraisal_events.evidence: Il passait la plus grande partie de son temps à envoyer à sa maîtresse des lettres et des dépêches... il lui écrivait : « Dis-moi ce que j'ai fait de mal »... c'est presque toujours le front soucieux et bien souvent les mains vides que je voyais Saint-Loup revenir de la poste.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator depicts Robert as anxiously dependent on a capricious mistress who withholds explanations and picks quarrels from a distance, reducing him to jealous suffering, self-doubt, and hollow errands to the post office.

appraisal_events.evidence: je me sentis un peu irrité de cet enfantillage qui m'étonnait tellement de sa part... si elle n'avait pas ce que je croyais lui être le plus étranger, de la coquetterie.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's own account shows him questioning his idealized image of his grandmother after seeing her dress up and hesitate over hairstyles for Saint-Loup's photograph, tentatively attributing to her a vanity he had thought foreign to her.

status_effects.explanation: Robert is locally weakened, shown as dependent on and subordinate to a mistress who mistreats him and leaves him in unresolved suffering and hatred.
The narrator's account mildly tempers his prior idealized view of his grandmother's detachment by noting an unexpected coquetry and childlike vanity.

ambiguities: Saint-Loup's mistress, whose manipulative behavior drives Robert's diminishment, is referred to only by generic descriptors ('sa maîtresse', 'son amie', 'l'amie de Saint-Loup') and never named in the passage; per scope rules she is not entered as a character, though she is causally central to E1.

The narrator's reassessment of his grandmother in E2 is explicitly framed as a tentative question ('je me demandais si...') rather than a settled judgment, so its narrative stance is left uncertain rather than fully endorsed.
